# Load Validation Data

```{r load-data}
agreement <- read_csv(here("data", "GPT_Russian_Agreement_18.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Loaded", nrow(agreement), "articles for coding validation.\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(names(agreement), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# Part 1: Confusion Matrices

```{r confusion-helper}
# Helper: build and save a confusion matrix heatmap
plot_confusion <- function(actual, predicted, actual_label, predicted_label,
                           title, filename, levels_order = NULL) {
  df <- data.frame(Actual = actual, Predicted = predicted, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Actual) & !is.na(Predicted))

  if (!is.null(levels_order)) {
    df$Actual <- factor(df$Actual, levels = levels_order)
    df$Predicted <- factor(df$Predicted, levels = levels_order)
  } else {
    all_levels <- sort(union(unique(df$Actual), unique(df$Predicted)))
    df$Actual <- factor(df$Actual, levels = all_levels)
    df$Predicted <- factor(df$Predicted, levels = all_levels)
  }

  counts <- df %>%
    count(Actual, Predicted, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    group_by(Actual) %>%
    mutate(pct = ifelse(sum(n) > 0, n / sum(n) * 100, 0)) %>%
    ungroup()

  total <- sum(counts$n)
  correct <- counts %>% filter(as.character(Actual) == as.character(Predicted)) %>% pull(n) %>% sum()
  accuracy <- round(correct / total * 100, 1)

  p <- ggplot(counts, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n)),
              size = 4, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue", name = "Count") +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = paste0("Overall agreement: ", accuracy, "% (n = ", total, ")"),
         x = predicted_label, y = actual_label) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    coord_fixed()

  ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_CODING, filename), p, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  print(p)
  invisible(p)
}
```

## Sentiment: Human Consensus vs GPT

```{r confusion-sentiment}
# Map numeric sentiment to labels
sentiment_levels <- c("Negative", "Neutral", "Positive")
sentiment_map <- c("-1" = "Negative", "0" = "Neutral", "1" = "Positive")

agreement <- agreement %>%
  mutate(
    human_align_label = sentiment_map[as.character(human_align)],
    GPT_Sentiment_label = sentiment_map[as.character(GPT_Sentiment)]
  )

plot_confusion(
  actual = agreement$human_align_label,
  predicted = agreement$GPT_Sentiment_label,
  actual_label = "Human Consensus",
  predicted_label = "GPT Sentiment",
  title = "Confusion Matrix: Sentiment (Human Consensus vs GPT)",
  filename = "confusion_sentiment.png",
  levels_order = sentiment_levels
)
```

# Part 1B: Krippendorff's Alpha

```{r krippendorff}
# --- Sentiment (ordinal, 3 coders) ---
sentiment_matrix <- rbind(
  as.numeric(agreement$sarah_russia_sentiment),
  as.numeric(agreement$donald_sentiment_recoding),
  as.numeric(agreement$GPT_Sentiment)
)
alpha_sentiment_3 <- kripp.alpha(sentiment_matrix, method = "ordinal")
cat("Krippendorff's alpha - Sentiment (3 coders, ordinal):", round(alpha_sentiment_3$value, 4), "\n")

# --- Sentiment (ordinal, human_align vs GPT) ---
sentiment_matrix_2 <- rbind(
  as.numeric(agreement$human_align),
  as.numeric(agreement$GPT_Sentiment)
)
alpha_sentiment_2 <- kripp.alpha(sentiment_matrix_2, method = "ordinal")
cat("Krippendorff's alpha - Sentiment (human consensus vs GPT, ordinal):", round(alpha_sentiment_2$value, 4), "\n")

# --- Topic (nominal, 3 coders) ---
# Encode topic categories as integers for kripp.alpha
all_topics <- sort(unique(c(agreement$sarah_topic, agreement$donald_topic, agreement$GPT_Topic)))
topic_to_int <- setNames(seq_along(all_topics), all_topics)

topic_matrix <- rbind(
  topic_to_int[agreement$sarah_topic],
  topic_to_int[agreement$donald_topic],
  topic_to_int[agreement$GPT_Topic]
)
alpha_topic <- kripp.alpha(topic_matrix, method = "nominal")
cat("Krippendorff's alpha - Topic (3 coders, nominal):", round(alpha_topic$value, 4), "\n")

# --- Russia-related (nominal, 3 coders) ---
russia_to_int <- c("yes" = 1, "no" = 2)

russia_matrix <- rbind(
  russia_to_int[agreement$sarah_russia_related],
  russia_to_int[agreement$donald_russia_related],
  russia_to_int[agreement$GPT_Russian_Involvement]
)
alpha_russia <- kripp.alpha(russia_matrix, method = "nominal")
cat("Krippendorff's alpha - Russia-Related (3 coders, nominal):", round(alpha_russia$value, 4), "\n")
```

```{r krippendorff-table}
# Summary table
alpha_summary <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Sentiment (3 coders)", "Sentiment (Human Consensus vs GPT)",
              "Topic (3 coders)", "Russia-Related (3 coders)"),
  Method = c("Ordinal", "Ordinal", "Nominal", "Nominal"),
  Coders = c("Sarah, Donald, GPT", "Human Consensus, GPT",
             "Sarah, Donald, GPT", "Sarah, Donald, GPT"),
  Alpha = c(round(alpha_sentiment_3$value, 4),
            round(alpha_sentiment_2$value, 4),
            round(alpha_topic$value, 4),
            round(alpha_russia$value, 4))
)

# Print as gt table
alpha_gt <- alpha_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Krippendorff's Alpha: Inter-Rater Reliability") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Alpha, decimals = 4)

alpha_gt

#gtsave(alpha_gt, file.path(FIGURES_CODING, "krippendorff_alpha.png"))
```

# Part 2: Region Map

```{r region-map, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Get world country polygons
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Define country groups — use admin names matching rnaturalearth
country_groups <- tribble(
  ~admin,                 ~group,          ~label,
  "Russia",               "Russia",        "Russia",
  "Ukraine",              "Ukraine",       "Ukraine",
  "Albania",              "NATO",          "Albania",
  "Hungary",              "NATO",          "Hungary",
  "Turkey",               "NATO",          "Turkey",
  "Armenia",              "Russia-Aligned","Armenia",
  "Azerbaijan",           "Russia-Aligned","Azerbaijan",
  "Kazakhstan",           "Russia-Aligned","Kazakhstan",
  "Belarus",              "Russia-Aligned","Belarus",
  "Republic of Serbia",   "Neutral",       "Serbia",
  "Kosovo",               "Neutral",       "Kosovo",
  "Moldova",              "Neutral",       "Moldova",
  "Georgia",              "Neutral",       "Georgia"
)

# Join groups to spatial data
map_data <- world %>%
  left_join(country_groups, by = "admin") %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

# Check which countries matched
cat("Matched countries:", paste(map_data$admin, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Define colors — steel tones for Russia/Ukraine/Neutral to match
group_colors <- c(
  "Russia"         = "indianred3",
  "Ukraine"        = "steelblue3",
  "NATO"           = "lightblue",
  "Russia-Aligned" = "#FF9999",
  "Neutral"        = "darkseagreen4"
)

# Compute label positions (centroids), then manually adjust overlapping ones
map_data_labels <- map_data %>%
  mutate(centroid = st_centroid(geometry)) %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[, 2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

# Countries that need arrows (small/overlapping)
arrow_countries <- c("Moldova", "Kosovo", "Albania", "Armenia", "Azerbaijan")

# Countries that need a nudged label but no arrow
nudge_countries <- c("Kazakhstan", "Russia")

# Manual label offsets
label_offsets <- tribble(
  ~label,        ~lon_off, ~lat_off,
  "Moldova",      -3,       -1.5,
  "Kosovo",       -2.5,     -1.2,
  "Albania",      -2.5,     -1,
  "Armenia",       2.5,     -2.5,
  "Azerbaijan",    3,        1.5,
  "Kazakhstan",    -8,       0,
  "Russia",        0,        0
)

# Arrow labels: offset + draw segment
arrow_labels <- map_data_labels %>%
  filter(label %in% arrow_countries) %>%
  left_join(label_offsets, by = "label") %>%
  mutate(
    label_lon = lon + lon_off,
    label_lat = lat + lat_off
  )

# Nudged labels: offset but no arrow
nudge_labels <- map_data_labels %>%
  filter(label %in% nudge_countries) %>%
  left_join(label_offsets, by = "label") %>%
  mutate(
    lon = lon + lon_off,
    lat = lat + lat_off
  )
# Russia's centroid is in Siberia (off-map), so hardcode a visible position
nudge_labels <- nudge_labels %>%
  mutate(
    lon = ifelse(label == "Russia", 45, lon),
    lat = ifelse(label == "Russia", 57, lat)
  )

# Direct labels: everything else, placed at centroid
direct_labels <- map_data_labels %>%
  filter(!(label %in% c(arrow_countries, nudge_countries)))

# Crop bounding box — tighter on the right to cut Kazakhstan, extended south for Turkey
bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = 15, xmax = 65, ymin = 28, ymax = 62), crs = st_crs(4326))

# Background countries for context (gray)
background <- world %>%
  st_crop(bbox) %>%
  filter(!(admin %in% country_groups$admin))

p_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = background, fill = "gray95", color = "gray70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = map_data, aes(fill = group), color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Direct labels for large countries
  geom_text(data = direct_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
            size = 3, fontface = "bold", color = "black") +
  # Nudged labels (no arrow) for countries whose centroid is off-screen or crowded
  geom_text(data = nudge_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
            size = 3, fontface = "bold", color = "black") +
  # Arrow labels for small/overlapping countries
  geom_segment(data = arrow_labels,
               aes(x = label_lon, y = label_lat, xend = lon, yend = lat),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = arrow_labels, aes(x = label_lon, y = label_lat, label = label),
            size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", color = "black",
            vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors, name = "Group") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(15, 65), ylim = c(35, 62), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Study Region: Russia's Near Abroad")

ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_CODING, "region_map.png"), p_map, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

p_map
```
